## Step 2: load the data

**Here, make sure you re-arrange the data so that all the data has a common time-period and has a common time frequency**

#### Processing the Data

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| code-fold: true

# Load necessary packages
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)

# Set folder path
data_path <- "DA_Jobs_vs_Econ"

# Load the datasets
fedfunds <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "FEDFUNDS.csv"))
indeed_da <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "indeed_data_analysis_job_postings.csv"))
pce <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "PCE.csv"))
ppi_info <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "PPI_Information.csv"))

# Convert date columns to Date
fedfunds[, 1] <- as.Date(fedfunds[, 1])
pce[, 1] <- as.Date(pce[, 1])
ppi_info[, 1] <- as.Date(ppi_info[, 1])

# Clean Indeed dataset separately
indeed_da$dateString <- as.Date(indeed_da$dateString)

# Keep only date and value columns
fedfunds <- fedfunds[, 1:2]
pce <- pce[, 1:2]
ppi_info <- ppi_info[, 1:2]

indeed_da <- indeed_da %>%
  filter(
    countryCode == "US",
    sectorName == "Data & Analytics",
    postingType == "TOTAL"
  ) %>%
  select(dateString, value)

# Rename columns
colnames(fedfunds) <- c("Date", "FedFundsRate")
colnames(indeed_da) <- c("Date", "DataAnalysisJobPostings")
colnames(pce) <- c("Date", "PCE")
colnames(ppi_info) <- c("Date", "PPIInformation")

# Function to convert any dataset to monthly data
to_monthly <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(Date = floor_date(Date, unit = "month")) %>%
    group_by(Date) %>%
    summarise(
      across(
        .cols = where(is.numeric),
        .fns = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Convert all datasets to monthly frequency
fedfunds_m <- to_monthly(fedfunds)
indeed_da_m <- to_monthly(indeed_da)
pce_m <- to_monthly(pce)
ppi_info_m <- to_monthly(ppi_info)

# Merge monthly datasets using only the common time period
merged_data <- Reduce(
  function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "Date", all = FALSE),
  list(
    indeed_da_m,
    fedfunds_m,
    pce_m,
    ppi_info_m
  )
)

# Sort by Date
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Remove any remaining missing values
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  filter(if_all(-Date, ~ !is.na(.x)))

# Display common time period
cat(
  "Common monthly time period:",
  as.character(min(merged_data$Date)),
  "to",
  as.character(max(merged_data$Date)),
  "\n"
)

# Display number of monthly observations
cat("Number of monthly observations:", nrow(merged_data), "\n")

# Display preview
kable(
  head(merged_data),
  caption = "Merged Monthly Dataset: Data Analysis Job Postings, Fed Funds Rate, PCE, and PPI Information"
)

# Assign final dataset
df <- merged_data
```

## Step 3: Convert to a ts() object

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| code-fold: true

# Load necessary packages
library(forecast)
library(lubridate)

# Use merged monthly dataset
df <- merged_data

# Make sure data are sorted by Date
df <- df[order(df$Date), ]

# Remove rows with missing values
df <- na.omit(df)

# Get start year and month from the first date
start_year <- year(min(df$Date))
start_month <- month(min(df$Date))

# Convert to time series object
# Monthly data: frequency = 12
df.ts <- ts(
  df[, -1],
  start = c(start_year, start_month),
  frequency = 12
)


```

## Step 5: EDA

Understand the correlation structure

### Lag Plots

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(forecast)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Make sure df is sorted by Date
df <- df[order(df$Date), ]

# Remove missing values
df <- na.omit(df)

# Get start year and month from your actual dataset
start_year <- year(min(df$Date))
start_month <- month(min(df$Date))

# Variables used in the current models
variables <- c(
  "DataAnalysisJobPostings",
  "FedFundsRate",
  "PCE",
  "PPIInformation"
)

# Cleaner names for plot titles and axis labels
variable_labels <- c(
  DataAnalysisJobPostings = "Data Analysis Job Postings",
  FedFundsRate = "Federal Funds Rate",
  PCE = "PCE",
  PPIInformation = "PPI Information"
)

# Function to create lag plot for one variable
create_lag_plot <- function(var_name, lags = 12) {
  
  ts_var <- ts(
    df[[var_name]],
    start = c(start_year, start_month),
    frequency = 12
  )
  
  p <- gglagplot(
    ts_var,
    do.lines = FALSE,
    lags = lags
  ) +
    ggtitle(paste("Lag Plots for", variable_labels[var_name])) +
    xlab(paste("Lagged", variable_labels[var_name])) +
    ylab(paste("Current", variable_labels[var_name])) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  ggplotly(p)
}

# Create lag plots
lag_plot_job_postings <- create_lag_plot("DataAnalysisJobPostings")
lag_plot_fedfunds <- create_lag_plot("FedFundsRate")
lag_plot_pce <- create_lag_plot("PCE")
lag_plot_ppi <- create_lag_plot("PPIInformation")

# Display lag plots
lag_plot_job_postings
lag_plot_fedfunds
lag_plot_pce
lag_plot_ppi
```

### Stationarity

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Load necessary package
library(tseries)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(lubridate)

# Make sure df is sorted by Date
df <- df[order(df$Date), ]

# Remove missing values
df <- na.omit(df)

# Get start year and month from your actual dataset
start_year <- year(min(df$Date))
start_month <- month(min(df$Date))

# Variables used in the current monthly model
variables <- c(
  "DataAnalysisJobPostings",
  "FedFundsRate",
  "PCE",
  "PPIInformation"
)

# Cleaner names
variable_labels <- c(
  DataAnalysisJobPostings = "Data Analysis Job Postings",
  FedFundsRate = "Federal Funds Rate",
  PCE = "PCE",
  PPIInformation = "PPI Information"
)

# Function to run ADF test for one variable
run_adf_test <- function(var_name) {
  
  ts_var <- ts(
    df[[var_name]],
    start = c(start_year, start_month),
    frequency = 12
  )
  
  adf_result <- adf.test(ts_var)
  
  data.frame(
    Variable = variable_labels[var_name],
    ADF_Statistic = as.numeric(adf_result$statistic),
    Lag_Order = as.numeric(adf_result$parameter),
    P_Value = adf_result$p.value,
    Conclusion = ifelse(
      adf_result$p.value < 0.05,
      "Stationary",
      "Non-stationary"
    )
  )
}

# Run ADF test for all variables
adf_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(variables, run_adf_test)
)

# Display results
knitr::kable(
  adf_results,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "ADF Test Results for Monthly Variables"
) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

if p-value \< 0.05 -\> reject unit root -\> stationary

if p-value \>= 0.05 -\> fail to reject unit root -\> non-stationary

## Step 6: Fitting the ARIMAX model using ’auto.arima()\`

We are using `auto.arima()` function to fit the ARIMAX model. Here we are predicting

```{r}
# Define the dependent variable
# Modeling Data Analysis job postings
y <- df.ts[, "DataAnalysisJobPostings"]

# Define external regressors
# Fed Funds Rate, PCE, and PPI Information
xreg <- df.ts[, c(
  "FedFundsRate",
  "PCE",
  "PPIInformation"
)]

# Fit the ARIMA model with external regressors
fit <- auto.arima(y, xreg = xreg)

# Display model summary
summary(fit)

# Model diagnostics
checkresiduals(fit)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 7: Fitting the model manually

### Regression + ARIMA(residuals of the Regression)

Instead of using the `auto.arima()` fucntion, let's fit the model manually. First let's fit the regression model to analyse the how these economical variables affect total vehicle sales in the US.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| code-fold: true
# Fit a linear regression model
model <- lm(
  DataAnalysisJobPostings ~ FedFundsRate + PCE + PPIInformation,
  data = df
)

# Display model summary
summary(model)

# Get start year and month from the common monthly dataset
start_year <- year(min(df$Date))
start_month <- month(min(df$Date))

# Extract residuals from the model
res.fit <- ts(
  residuals(model),
  start = c(start_year, start_month),
  frequency = 12
)

ggAcf(res.fit)
```

## Step 8: Model Search for the residuals

1.  This is just checking:

```{r}
auto.arima(res.fit)
```

### 2. Manual Search

**Manual parameter search through differencing ordinarily and seasonally:**

#### Apply First-Order Differencing only

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#| code-fold: true

###### Apply First-Order Differencing ######

first_diff <- diff(res.fit)

p1<-ggAcf(first_diff)+

  ggtitle("ACF of First Differenced Residuals")

p2<-ggPacf(first_diff) +

  ggtitle("PACF of First Differenced Residuals")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

it is apparent that no ordinary differencing is needed, so d=0 can be a possible candidate.

##### Check the ACF of the residuals

I'm doing this step since it shows above d=0, but id d=1, you don't need to check this.

```{r}
ggAcf(res.fit)+

  ggtitle("ACF of Residuals of the fit")

ggPacf(res.fit) +

  ggtitle("PACF of Residuals of the fit")
```

from ACF plot -\> q= 1,2,3,4 and from PACF plot -\> p=1

#### Apply Seasonal Differencing only

```{r}

###### Apply Seasonal Differencing (Lag = 12) only ######

seasonal_diff <- diff(res.fit, lag = 12)

###### Plot ACF and PACF for the Differenced Series ######

p3 <- ggAcf(seasonal_diff) +

  ggtitle("ACF of Seasonally Differenced Residuals") +

  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggPacf(seasonal_diff) +

  ggtitle("PACF of Seasonally Differenced Residuals") +

  theme_minimal()

# Display plots
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p3, p4, ncol = 2)
```

from PACF: P=1, and from ACF: Q=1, since we seasonaly differenced once: D=1

```{r}
###### Apply Seasonal Differencing (Lag = 12) on Top of First-Order Differencing ######

seasonal_diff <- diff(first_diff, lag = 12)

###### Plot ACF and PACF for the Differenced Series ######

p1 <- ggAcf(seasonal_diff) +

  ggtitle("ACF of Seasonally Differenced Residuals") +

  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggPacf(seasonal_diff) +

  ggtitle("PACF of Seasonally Differenced Residuals") +

  theme_minimal()

# Display plots

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)

```

Here d=1, D=1, P=1, Q=1

## Step 9: Parameter tuning

**Let's run through a parameter search using the above selected parameters in the ARIMA model:**

So overall collection of parameters: d=0,1, p=1, q=1:4, D=1, P=1, Q=1

#### This is in case you DON'T have seasonality.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Load necessary libraries
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)


# Define parameter ranges
p_range <- 1:4
d_range <- 0:1
q_range <- 1:1  # 

# Calculate total combinations
n_combinations <- length(p_range) * length(d_range) * length(q_range)

# Create an empty matrix to store results
results_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_combinations, ncol = 6)

# Initialize index for matrix row
i <- 1

# Loop through combinations of ARIMA model parameters
for (d in d_range) {
  for (p in p_range) {
    for (q in q_range)

    # Fit ARIMA model with specified (p,d,q)
    model <- Arima(res.fit, order = c(p, d, q), include.drift = TRUE)

    # Store model parameters and AIC/BIC/AICc values in matrix
    results_matrix[i, ] <- c(p, d, q, model$aic, model$bic, model$aicc)

    # Increment row index
    i <- i + 1
  }
}

# Convert matrix to data frame
results_df <- as.data.frame(results_matrix)
colnames(results_df) <- c("p", "d", "q", "AIC", "BIC", "AICc")

# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Create table of top 10 models based on AIC
top_results_df <- results_df |>
  arrange(AIC) |>
  head(10)

# Find the row with the lowest AIC in the top 10 table
highlight_row <- which.min(top_results_df$AIC)

# Generate kable table with highlighting for the row with the lowest AIC
knitr::kable(
  top_results_df,
  align = "c",
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Top 10 ARIMA Models Based on AIC"
) |>
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) |>
  row_spec(
    highlight_row,
    bold = TRUE,
    background = "#FFFF99"
  )
```

#### This is when you have seasonality.

## SARIMA model

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Load libraries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(forecast)
library(dplyr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Check time series object
# ------------------------------------------------------------

#frequency(ts_unemployment)
#length(ts_unemployment)
#sum(is.na(ts_unemployment))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SARIMA Model Comparison Function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

SARIMA.c <- function(p1, p2, q1, q2, P1, P2, Q1, Q2, data) {
  
  # Differencing orders and seasonal period
  d <- 0
  D <- 1
  s <- 12
  
  # Store results
  results <- list()
  i <- 1
  
  # Iterate over parameter ranges
  for (p in p1:p2) {
    for (q in q1:q2) {
      for (P in P1:P2) {
        for (Q in Q1:Q2) {
          
          # Avoid overly complex models
          if (p + d + q + P + D + Q <= 10) {
            
            model <- tryCatch(
              {
                forecast::Arima(
                  data,
                  order = c(p, d, q),
                  seasonal = list(order = c(P, D, Q), period = s)
                )
              },
              error = function(e) {
                message(
                  "Model failed: ARIMA(",
                  p, ",", d, ",", q, ") x (",
                  P, ",", D, ",", Q, ")[", s, "] : ",
                  e$message
                )
                return(NULL)
              }
            )
            
            if (!is.null(model)) {
              results[[i]] <- data.frame(
                p = p,
                d = d,
                q = q,
                P = P,
                D = D,
                Q = Q,
                AIC = model$aic,
                BIC = model$bic,
                AICc = model$aicc
              )
              
              i <- i + 1
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # If no models worked, stop with clear message
  if (length(results) == 0) {
    stop("No SARIMA models were successfully fitted. Check the error messages above.")
  }
  
  # Combine results
  results_df <- bind_rows(results)
  
  return(results_df)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Run SARIMA Model Comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------

#q= 1,2,3,4 and p=1, D=1, Q=1, P=1
output <- SARIMA.c(
  p1 = 0, p2 = 1,
  q1 = 1, q2 = 4,
  P1 = 0, P2 = 1,
  Q1 = 0, Q2 = 1,
  data = res.fit
)


# Optional: show top models
results_top<-output |>
  arrange(AIC) |>
  head(10)

highlight_row <- which.min(results_top$AIC)

knitr::kable(
  results_top,
  align = "c",
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Top 10 SARIMA Models Based on AIC"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(
    highlight_row,
    bold = TRUE,
    background = "#FFFF99"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify Best Models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

best_models <- bind_rows(
  "Best by AIC" = output |> slice_min(AIC, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  "Best by BIC" = output |> slice_min(BIC, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE),
  .id = "Selection_Criterion"
)

knitr::kable(
  best_models,
  align = "c",
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Best SARIMA Models Based on AIC and BIC"
) |>
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )

```

## Step 10: Write down the Possible Models

ARIMA(1,0,1)

ARIMA(3,1,1)

ARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)12

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Load libraries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(forecast)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross-Validation Settings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

y <- res.fit
n <- length(y)

# Initial training window:
# approximately one-third of the observations,
# rounded down to a complete number of years
k <- floor(n / 3 / 12) * 12

# Forecast 12 months ahead at every forecast origin
h <- 12

# Only use origins with all 12 future observations available
n_origins <- n - k - h + 1

if (k < 24) {
  warning("The initial training window contains fewer than two seasonal cycles.")
}

if (n_origins < 1) {
  stop("There are not enough observations for 12-step cross-validation.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Initialize Forecast Error Matrices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Rows represent forecast origins
# Columns represent forecast horizons 1 through 12
errors_model1 <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_origins,
  ncol = h
)

errors_model2 <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_origins,
  ncol = h
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Expanding-Window Cross-Validation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (i in seq_len(n_origins)) {
  
  # Last observation included in the current training sample
  train_end <- k + i - 1
  
  # Expanding training set
  xtrain <- window(
    y,
    end = time(y)[train_end]
  )
  
  # Next 12 observed values
  xtest <- as.numeric(
    y[(train_end + 1):(train_end + h)]
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 1: SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12]
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  fit1 <- tryCatch(
    Arima(
      xtrain,
      order = c(1, 0, 1),
      seasonal = list(
        order = c(0, 1, 1),
        period = 12
      ),
      method = "ML"
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (!is.null(fit1)) {
    forecast1 <- forecast(fit1, h = h)
    
    errors_model1[i, ] <-
      as.numeric(forecast1$mean) - xtest
  }
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 2: SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,1,1)[12]
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  fit2 <- tryCatch(
    Arima(
      xtrain,
      order = c(1, 0, 1),
      seasonal = list(
        order = c(1, 1, 1),
        period = 12
      ),
      method = "ML"
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (!is.null(fit2)) {
    forecast2 <- forecast(fit2, h = h)
    
    errors_model2[i, ] <-
      as.numeric(forecast2$mean) - xtest
  }
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Horizon-Specific RMSE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rmse_model1 <- sqrt(
  colMeans(errors_model1^2, na.rm = TRUE)
)

rmse_model2 <- sqrt(
  colMeans(errors_model2^2, na.rm = TRUE)
)

rmse_table <- data.frame(
  Horizon = 1:h,
  `SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12]` = rmse_model1,
  `SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,1,1)[12]` = rmse_model2,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Display RMSE Table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

kable(
  rmse_table,
  format = "html",
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Rolling-Origin RMSE by Forecast Horizon"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c(
      "striped",
      "hover",
      "condensed",
      "responsive"
    )
  )
```

## Step 11: Model Diagnostics

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(astsa)
library(forecast)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Make sure res.fit is a monthly time series
# This assumes res.fit was already created from your model residuals
# frequency(res.fit) should be 12

frequency(res.fit)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(345)

###### Fit ARIMA(1,0,1) Model ######
model_1_output <- capture.output(
  sarima(res.fit, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 12)
)

###### Fit ARIMA(3,1,1) Model ######
model_2_output <- capture.output(
  sarima(res.fit, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 12)
)

###### Fit SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12] Model ######
model_3_output <- capture.output(
  sarima(res.fit, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 12)
)

###### Extract and Print Relevant Output ######
extract_model_output <- function(model_output, model_name) {
  
  start_line <- grep("Coefficients", model_output)
  
  if (length(start_line) == 0) {
    start_line <- 1
  }
  
  end_line <- length(model_output)
  
  cat("\n###", model_name, "###\n")
  cat(model_output[start_line:end_line], sep = "\n")
}

###### Print Model Outputs ######
extract_model_output(model_1_output, "ARIMA(1,0,1)")
extract_model_output(model_2_output, "ARIMA(3,1,1)")
extract_model_output(model_3_output, "SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12]")
```

#### Change these interpretations accordingly:

For both of above models:

The **Residual Plot** shows nearly consistent fluctuation around zero, suggesting that the residuals are nearly stationary with a constant mean and finite variance over time.

The **Autocorrelation Function (ACF)** of the residuals reveals no significant autocorrelations indicating a good model.

The **Q-Q Plot** indicates that the residuals follow a near-normal distribution, with minor deviations at the tails, which is typical in time series data.

The **Ljung-Box Test** p-values remain mostly above the 0.05 significance level, implying a nearly good fit.

**Coefficient Significance**: For the first model the coefficient of sma1 is not significant at 5% Significance level, but for the second model all variables are significant.

## Step 12: Model Equation

```{r}

# Define the dependent variable
# Modeling Data Analysis Job Postings
y <- df.ts[, "DataAnalysisJobPostings"]

# Define external regressors
# Fed Funds Rate, PCE, and PPI Information
xreg <- df.ts[, c(
  "FedFundsRate",
  "PCE",
  "PPIInformation"
)]


# Fit final ARIMAX model:
# ARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12] with external regressors
fit <- Arima(
  y,
  order = c(1, 0, 1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(0, 1, 1), period = 12),
  xreg = xreg
)

# Display model summary
summary(fit)
```

#### Model Equation

::: {.callout-note title="Model Equation for SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12]"}
$$y_t  =\beta x_t+n_t $$

$$\Phi_P\left(B^s\right) \varphi(B) \nabla_s^D \nabla^d n_t=\delta+\Theta_Q\left(B^s\right) \theta(B) w_t$$

With the parameters from the model:

$$y_t  =\beta x_t+n_t $$

$$y_t  =-8.97 FedFundsRate +0.0064 PCE -0.8 PPIInformation + n_t $$ Here, $y_t$ is Data Analysis Job Postings.

With ARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)\[12\] errors:

$$(1-\phi_1B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+\theta_1B)(1+\Theta_1B^{12})w_t$$

$$(1-0.98B) (1-B^12) n_t=\left(1+0.8B)(1-0.68 B^{12}\right) w_t$$
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Model Equation: Regression with SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12] Errors"}
The model can be written as:

$$y_t = \beta_1 X_{1t} + \beta_2 X_{2t} + \beta_3 X_{3t} + n_t$$

where (y_t) is **Data Analysis Job Postings**, and (n_t) is the ARIMA error term.

Using the estimated regression coefficients:

$$y_t =
-8.9769(\text{FedFundsRate}_t)
+0.0064(\text{PCE}_t)
-0.8042(\text{PPIInformation}_t)
+n_t$$

The error term follows:

$$\Phi_P(B^{12})\varphi(B)\nabla_{12}^{1}\nabla^{0}n_t
=
\Theta_Q(B^{12})\theta(B)w_t$$

For the selected model:

$$(1-\phi_1B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+\theta_1B)(1+\Theta_1B^{12})w_t$$

Substituting the estimated ARIMA coefficients:

$$(1-0.9824B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+0.8091B)(1-0.6881B^{12})w_t$$
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Model Equation: Regression with SARIMA(1,0,1)(0,1,1)[12] Errors"}
The model can be written as:

$$y_t = \beta_1 X_{1t} + \beta_2 X_{2t} + \beta_3 X_{3t} + n_t$$

where ($y_t$) is **Software Job Postings**, and (n_t) is the SARIMA error term.

Using the estimated regression coefficients:

$$y_t =
-12.973(\text{FedFundsRate}_t)
+0.0047(\text{PCE}_t)
-1.3354(\text{PPIInformation}_t)
+n_t$$

The error term follows:

$$\Phi_P(B^{12})\varphi(B)\nabla_{12}^{1}\nabla^{0}n_t
=
\Theta_Q(B^{12})\theta(B)w_t$$

For the selected model:

$$(1-\phi_1B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+\theta_1B)(1+\Theta_1B^{12})w_t$$

Substituting the estimated ARIMA coefficients:

$$(1-0.9881B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+0.8037B)(1-0.9997B^{12})w_t$$
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Model Equation: Overall Job Openings with SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] Errors"}

The model can be written as:

$$
y_t = \beta_1 X_{1t} + \beta_2 X_{2t} + \beta_3 X_{3t} + n_t
$$

where \(y_t\) represents **Overall Job Openings**, and \(n_t\) is the SARIMA error term.

Using the estimated regression coefficients:

$$
y_t =
-1.4234(\text{FEDFUNDS}_t)
+0.0069(\text{PCE}_t)
+0.2231(\text{PPI\_Information}_t)
+n_t
$$

The error term follows a SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] structure:

$$
\nabla^{1}\nabla_{12}^{1}n_t
=
\theta(B)\Theta(B^{12})w_t
$$

For the selected model:

$$
(1-B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+\theta_1B)(1+\Theta_1B^{12})w_t
$$

Substituting the estimated ARIMA coefficients:

$$
(1-B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+0.8082B)(1-0.6614B^{12})w_t
$$

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Model Equation: Unemployment in the Information Sector with SARIMA(1,1,3)(0,1,1)[12] Errors"}

The model can be written as:

$$
y_t = \beta_1 X_{1t} + \beta_2 X_{2t} + \beta_3 X_{3t} + n_t
$$

where \(y_t\) represents **Unemployment in the Information Sector**, and \(n_t\) is the SARIMA error term.

Using the estimated regression coefficients:

$$
y_t =
-8.9922(\text{FedFundsRate}_t)
-0.0536(\text{PCE}_t)
+2.8742(\text{PPIInformation}_t)
+n_t
$$

The error term follows a SARIMA(1,1,3)(0,1,1)[12] structure:

$$
\varphi(B)\nabla^{1}\nabla_{12}^{1}n_t
=
\theta(B)\Theta(B^{12})w_t
$$

For the selected model:

$$
(1-\phi_1B)(1-B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1+\theta_1B+\theta_2B^2+\theta_3B^3)(1+\Theta_1B^{12})w_t
$$

Substituting the estimated ARIMA coefficients:

$$
(1-0.1720B)(1-B)(1-B^{12})n_t
=
(1-0.4624B+0.1175B^2-0.2795B^3)(1-1.0000B^{12})w_t
$$

:::

# Final Forecasting

First, forecast individual exogenous variables using auto.arima() models.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| code-fold: true


# Fit ARIMA model to each external regressor

# Federal Funds Rate
FedFunds_fit <- auto.arima(xreg[, "FedFundsRate"])
# summary(FedFunds_fit)
fFedFunds <- forecast(FedFunds_fit, h = 36)

# PCE
PCE_fit <- auto.arima(xreg[, "PCE"])
# summary(PCE_fit)
fPCE <- forecast(PCE_fit, h = 36)

# PPI Information
PPI_fit <- auto.arima(xreg[, "PPIInformation"])
# summary(PPI_fit)
fPPI <- forecast(PPI_fit, h = 36)

# Create future external regressor matrix using forecasted values
fxreg <- cbind(
  FedFundsRate = fFedFunds$mean,
  PCE = fPCE$mean,
  PPIInformation = fPPI$mean
)
```

using the forecast individual exogenous variables using auto.arima() models, we will forecast our y variable.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| code-fold: true
# Forecast Data Analysis Job Postings using future external regressors
fcast <- forecast(
  fit,
  xreg = fxreg,
  h = 36
)

# Static forecast plot
autoplot(fcast) +
  ggtitle("Forecast of Data Analysis Job Postings for the Next 36 Months") +
  xlab("Year") +
  ylab("Data Analysis Job Postings Index") +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(plotly)
library(lubridate)

# Create future monthly dates
future_dates <- seq(
  from = max(df$Date) %m+% months(1),
  by = "month",
  length.out = 36
)

# Create a data frame from the forecast object
fcast_df <- data.frame(
  Date = future_dates,
  Forecast = as.numeric(fcast$mean),
  Lower80 = as.numeric(fcast$lower[, 1]),
  Upper80 = as.numeric(fcast$upper[, 1]),
  Lower95 = as.numeric(fcast$lower[, 2]),
  Upper95 = as.numeric(fcast$upper[, 2])
)

# Convert the original series for plotting
orig_df <- data.frame(
  Date = df$Date,
  Actual = as.numeric(y)
)

# Plotly interactive plot
plot_ly() |>
  add_lines(
    data = orig_df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~Actual,
    name = "Actual"
  ) |>
  add_lines(
    data = fcast_df,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~Forecast,
    name = "Forecast"
  ) |>
  add_ribbons(
    data = fcast_df,
    x = ~Date,
    ymin = ~Lower95,
    ymax = ~Upper95,
    name = "95% CI",
    opacity = 0.2,
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_ribbons(
    data = fcast_df,
    x = ~Date,
    ymin = ~Lower80,
    ymax = ~Upper80,
    name = "80% CI",
    opacity = 0.3,
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = "Forecast of Data Analysis Job Postings for the Next 36 Months",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Data Analysis Job Postings Index")
  )
```
